Directions: In the following question, a part of the sentence has been highlighted. You need to identify which of the given options can replace the highlighted part and make the sentence grammatically and contextually correct. In case the highlighted part is correct, mark (e) as your answer.


The findings are revealing a significant insight into the behavior of molecular structures that are existing in multiple states, fluctuating between them rapidly.
questions.explanation: The present continuous form "are revealing" is inappropriate for the context. The present perfect "have revealed" is more suitable as it denotes a link between the past findings and the present insight. Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

questions.explanation: The past continuous “was having” is incorrect due to subject-verb disagreement, and it also fails to convey the completion of action in the past. “Had” correctly implies the completion and the implications that had already occurred. Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Direction: Rearrange the following five segments (A),(B),(C),(D) and (E) in the proper sequence to form a meaningful paragraph; then answer the questions given below them.


A. This time lag is needed to ensure that there is no interference – the signals going back and forth should not cross paths, similar to two people talking to each other at the same time, without pausing to listen to the other.

B. Full-duplex antennas consist of a transmitter and a receiver to send and receive radio signals.

C. According to IISc, such full-duplex antennas are particularly helpful for applications that require almost instantaneous relay of commands, like driverless cars.

D. Researchers at the Indian Institute of Science are working on designing antennas that can empower 6G technology,which is instrumental in realising efficient V2X (Vehicle to communications).

E. Traditional radio transceivers are half duplex, which means that they either use signals of different frequencies for sending and receiving or there is a time lag between the signal transmitted and the signal received.

Which is the first sentence according to the paragraph?
questions.explanation:
"D starts by highlighting Indian Institute of Science's research on 6G antennas for V2X communications. C follows, emphasizing their relevance for swift command relay in applications like driverless cars. B explains the structure of full-duplex antennas, contrasting with E, which contrasts them with half-duplex systems. Finally, A concludes by explaining the necessity of time lag in full-duplex setups to prevent signal interference, forming the logical sequence DCBEA."

Therefore, option A is the correct answer.

questions.question: Which of the following option can be inferred from the given passage?
options: Live in peace, not in search of it
questions.explanation: The most appropriate option which can be inferred from the above passage is 'Live in peace, not in search of it'. The whole passage talks about how we should stick to peace and be in a peaceful state of mind, then everything will fall in place, sooner or later. In this world everyone wants to live in peace but no one likes to live in search of it, sometimes lack of knowledge and inner powers make many of us strive and struggle to get peace from wrong sources. Therefore true peace remains a distant dream.

questions.question: What is the tone of the author in the passage?
questions.explanation: The tone of the given passage is ‘DOGMATIC’. DOGMATIC means when the author has some firm beliefs and perspective regarding particular aspects of life and is assertive regarding his opinions, he uses a dogmatic tone to convey his viewpoint. Other options can be eliminated, as these are not relevant to the passage. CRITICAL tone means a fault-finding attitude of the author; in a negative sense. VINDICTIVE tone means someone who holds a grudge and who always tries to get back at people who they think have wronged them in some way. SARCASTIC tone means using remarks that clearly mean the opposite of what you say, in order to hurt someone’s feelings or to humorously criticize something. BIASED tone means a prejudice against something an author is writing about.

questions.question: As given in the passage, which of the following word is the synonym of the word ‘delineation’?
questions.explanation: ‘Delineation’ is the synonym of ‘description’. DELINEATION means the action of describing or marking the edge of something. Electrification – the action or process of charging something with electricity. Discretionary – available for use at the discretion of the user. Administration - the group of people or part of a company that organizes or controls something. Position – the place where somebody/something is or should be.

questions.question:
Directions: Read the sentence to find out whether there is any grammatical or idiomatic error in it. The error, if any, will be in two parts of the sentence. Mark the parts with the error as your answer. If there is no error, mark (E). (Ignore errors of punctuation, if any)

Computer viruses, like there(A)/ biological counterparts, can(B)/ spread quickly though interconnected systems,(C)/ causing digital havoc.(D)
questions.explanation:
Error in Part A: "there" should be replaced with "their."
The possessive pronoun "their" is used to indicate ownership or belonging. In this context, it refers to the possession of biological counterparts. "There" is used to indicate a place or location and doesn't fit in this context.

Error in Part C: "though" should be replaced with "through."
"Through" is the correct preposition to use in this context to indicate the means by which computer viruses spread. "Though" is unrelated to the intended meaning.
Hence, option (C) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Directions: Read the sentence to find out whether there is any grammatical or idiomatic error in it. The error, if any, will be in two parts of the sentence. Mark the parts with the error as your answer. If there is no error, mark (E). (Ignore errors of punctuation, if any)

Renewable energy sources,(A)/ such as solar and wind power,(B)/ is gaining popularity due to their(C)/ environmental benefits and(C)/ decreased reliance on fossil fuels.(D)
questions.explanation:
Error in Part C: "Renewable energy sources" is a plural subject, so the verb should also be plural. "Is" should be replaced with "are."
Error in Part D: ‘decreased’ will be replaced with decreasing’ to maintain parallelism.
Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Directions: Read the sentence to find out whether there is any grammatical or idiomatic error in it. The error, if any, will be in two parts of the sentence. Mark the parts with the error as your answer. If there is no error, mark (E). (Ignore errors of punctuation, if any)

The Great Barrier Reef,(A)/ one of the world's most stunning(B)/ natural wonder, is threatened by coral bleaching(C)/ caused of rising ocean temperatures.(D)
questions.explanation:
Error in Part C: ‘wonders’ will be used in place of ‘wonder’ since ‘one of the’ takes plural nouns.
Error in Part D: "caused of" should be replaced with "caused by."
The correct preposition to use in this context is "by," not "of." "Caused by" indicates the cause or origin of the coral bleaching.
Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Directions: Read the sentence to find out whether there is any grammatical or idiomatic error in it. The error, if any, will be in two parts of the sentence. Mark the parts with the error as your answer. If there is no error, mark (E). (Ignore errors of punctuation, if any)

questions.explanation:

"Quantum computing" is a singular subject, so the verb should be in the singular form "holds" instead of "hold."

Error in Part D:  "most unique" is redundant. The word "unique" already signifies something that is one of a kind, so adding "most" before it is unnecessary.
Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Directions: In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select ‘No Error’.

Even though the wind(A)/ was enough strong to knock(B)/ down the trees,(C)/ the house remained standing.(D)/ No error (E)
questions.explanation:
In part (B), the word "strong" is incorrectly placed.

  • When "enough" modifies an adjective, it should come after the adjective.
  • The correct word here should be "strong enough", as "enough" is needed to modify "strong" and show that the wind had sufficient strength.
    • Examples:
      • Incorrect: She is enough tall to reach the top shelf.
      • Correct: She is tall enough to reach the top shelf.

Corrected Sentence: Even though the wind was strong enough to knock down the trees, the house remained standing.

Hence, option B is the correct choice.

questions.question:
Direction: In the following question, a sentence is given, divided into four parts. Out of the four parts, one part may contain an error. Mark the part having an error as your answer. If none of the parts contain an error, mark “No error” as your answer.

From 1885 to 1887 he served as assistant solicitor(a)/ of Hamilton County, and in the latter year(b)/ was appointed as judge of the Superior Court(c)/ of Ohio to fill a vacancy.(d)/ No error(e)
questions.explanation:
Correct Answer: Option C (c)

  • In part (c), "appointed as judge" is incorrect.
  • The correct phrase should be "appointed judge" without the preposition "as."
  • The verb "appointed" is directly followed by the noun (in this case, "judge") without the need for "as."
  • After verbs like "appoint, elect, consider, call, name, choose, etc.", do not use "as." Simply use the verb followed by the noun or role. 
    • Examples:
      • Incorrect: He was elected as the president of the club.
      • Correct: He was elected president of the club.

Corrected Sentence: From 1885 to 1887 he served as assistant solicitor of Hamilton County, and in the latter year was appointed judge of the Superior Court of Ohio to fill a vacancy.

questions.question: The average age of 50 students is 18 years. The average age of the first 30 students is 19 years. The average age of the last 10 students is 15 years. Find the average age of the remaining 10 students.
questions.explanation:
Let's call the total age of the 50 students as "A". The total age of the first 30 students is

30 \(\times\) 19 = 570 years.

The total age of the last 10 students is 10 \(\times\) 15 = 150 years.

So, A = 570 + 150 + total age of the remaining 10 students = 570 + 150 + 10x (where x is the average age of the remaining 10 students)

We know that the average age of 50 students is 18, so A = 50 \(\times\) 18 = 900.

By substituting the values we have, we get:

900 = 570 + 150 + 10x

900 - 570 - 150 = 10x

180 = 10x

x = 18

So, the average age of the remaining 10 students is 18 years.

questions.question: Pipes P and Q can fill a cistern in 30 and 40 minutes respectively. Pipe R can empty the filled cistern in 60 minutes. If all the three pipes are kept open for one minute each, how much time will the pipes take to fill the cistern?
questions.explanation:
Given cistern P and Q can fill the tank in 30 and 40 minutes respectively. Therefore,

part filled by tap P in 1 minute = \(\frac{1}{30}\)

part filled by tap Q in 1 minute = \(\frac{1}{40}\ \)

Tap R can empty the cistern in 60 minutes. Therefore,

part emptied by tap R in 1 minute = \(\frac{1}{60}\)

Net part filled by Pipes P, Q, R together in 1 minute \(= \ \left\lbrack \frac{1}{30} + \frac{1}{40} - \frac{1}{60} \right\rbrack = \frac{5}{120}\text{ }\)

\(= \frac{1}{24}\)

i.e., the cistern can be filled in 24 minutes.

Short Trick:

P = 30 min
Q = 40 min
R (emptying) = 60 min
Take LCM of 30, 40, 60 = 120 units (total work = 120 units)
Work done per minute 
P = 120 ÷ 30 = 4 units/min
Q = 120 ÷ 40 = 3 units/min
R = 120 ÷ 60 = 2 units/min (negative because it empties)
All three together per minute = 4 + 3 − 2 = 5 units/min
Total work = 120 units
So, time = 120 ÷ 5 = 24 minutes
Final Answer:
The tank will be filled in 24 minutes.

Eight people Z, Y, X, P, Q, R, A and C are sitting around a circular table, some of them are facing inside and some of them are facing outside the table. A sits third to the left of P. There are two people sitting between A and Z. X sits second to the right of Z. Q sits just to the left of X. C sits opposite to Q. Y sits second to the left of C. Y faces inside the table. R sits third to the right of Y. Q and Y face opposite directions to each other. A and R face opposite directions to Q.

 

As many people are sitting between P and C as between Q and …… ?
questions.explanation:
A sits third to the left of P.

There are two people sitting between A and Z.

X sits second to the right of Z.

Q sits just to the left of X.
C sits opposite to Q.

Y sits second to the left of C.

Y faces inside the table.
R sits third to the right of Y.

Q and Y face opposite directions to each other.

A and R face opposite directions to Q.

questions.question: If 1 is subtracted from an odd digit and 2 is added to an even digit of the number “694523715”, then which of the following numbers are repeated more than two times?
questions.explanation:
6 9 4 5 2 3 7 1 5

After 1 is subtracted from an odd digit and 2 is added to an even digit of the number we get,

8 8 6 4 4 2 6 0 4

questions.question:
Directions: Study the following data carefully and answer the questions accordingly.

Statement: T < S, K > G, G < Z, K > S

Conclusion:

I. Z ≤S

II. Z > S
options: Both conclusions I and II are true
Neither conclusion I nor II is true
Either conclusion I or II is true
questions.explanation:
Given-

T < S, K > G, G < Z, K > S

T < S < K > G < Z

I. Z ≤S ( False)

II. Z > S (False)

(But They are complimentary pair) so Either Z ≤S or Z > S

questions.question:
In the given questions, assuming the given statements to be true. Find which of the given two conclusions number I and II is/are definitely true and give your answer accordingly.


Statement: Z > H < V < M, Q > M < R

Conclusion:

I. Q > H

II. Z < R
options: Both conclusions I and II are true
Neither conclusion I nor II is true
Either conclusion I or II is true
questions.explanation:
Q > M > V > H (I. Q > H) True
Z > H < V < M < R (II. Z < R) False
